l: oaths of the ancients, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: Akish's kindred swore by the God of heaven, the heavens, the earth, and their heads to assist him and keep his matters secret. Akish administered ancient oaths that had been handed down from those who sought power.

l: the secret combinations of Akish and his friends, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: Akish and his kindred formed a secret combination through oaths and fair promises. Such combinations are described as abominable and wicked, built to gain power and gain, and destined to cause destruction.

l: power, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: The secret combination was formed to obtain power and was kept up by the power of the devil. Moroni warned that combinations seeking power would overthrow freedom and bring destruction.

l: power and gain, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: The combinations were built to obtain gain as well as power. Nations that uphold them until they spread over the nation are warned that they will be destroyed.

l: murder, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: The oaths supported murder, plunder, lying, and other wickedness. The Lord forbids the shedding of blood, and the blood of those slain is described as crying from the ground for vengeance.

l: freedom, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: Secret combinations seek to overthrow the freedom of all lands, nations, and countries. Their spread brings the destruction of all people.

l: The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: This unit concerns the overthrow of Omer’s kingdom through the secret combinations of Akish and his friends, followed by Jared’s reign, Akish’s conspiracies, and a war that destroys nearly all the people. Omer escapes with most of his family, later returns, and is succeeded by Emer, whose house prospers greatly under the Lord’s blessings. Coriantum, Com, and Heth then reign in succession, while wickedness, famine, poisonous serpents, and destruction return to the land. After the people repent and humble themselves, the Lord sends rain and preserves them from famine.

l: Akish, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: Akish and his friends overthrow the kingdom of Omer. Akish marries Jared’s daughter, arranges the murder of his father-in-law through a secret society, reigns in Jared’s place, imprisons and starves one of his sons to death, and wars with his other sons.

l: Omer, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: Omer is warned by the Lord in a dream to leave the land, and he travels with his family to Ablom, except for Jared and his family. He later dwells with Nimrah and is restored to the land of his inheritance, where he anoints Emer as king before dying in old age.

l: Jared, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: Jared is anointed king over the people through wickedness and gives his daughter to Akish as a wife. Akish has Jared murdered while he sits upon his throne giving audience to his people.

l: Emer, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: Emer is anointed king by Omer and reigns in his stead. Under Emer’s reign, the house of Emer prospers exceedingly, and Emer later anoints Coriantum to reign after him.

l: Coriantum, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: Coriantum succeeds Emer, builds many mighty cities, and administers good to his people. He has no children until he is exceedingly old, then takes a young maid to wife and begets sons and daughters, including Com.

l: Heth, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: Heth is begotten by Com and later embraces the secret plans of old to destroy his father. He dethrones and kills Com with his own sword, then reigns in his stead and commands actions against the prophets.

l: the Lord, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: The Lord warns Omer to depart in a dream, takes the curse from the land during Emer’s reign, and pours blessings upon the land. He sends prophets, causes the poisonous serpents to stop pursuing the people, and sends rain after the people repent and humble themselves.

l: the house of Omer, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: The house of Omer includes Omer’s family and those who flee with him. It survives the destruction of nearly all the people and later dwells with Omer after Nimrah flees the land.

l: the sons of Akish, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: The sons of Akish win the hearts of the people after swearing to do iniquity according to Akish’s desires. They offer money to draw most of the people after them and enter into a war with Akish.

l: people, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: The people become corrupted by the secret society, and nearly all of them are destroyed in the war between Akish and his sons. Later, the people reject and persecute the prophets, suffer dearth and poisonous serpents, and eventually repent and cry unto the Lord.

l: the secret combinations of Akish and his friends, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: The secret combinations of Akish and his friends overthrow the kingdom of Omer. The spreading of the wicked and secret society corrupts the hearts of all the people.

l: land of promise, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: The land is restored to Omer and later prospers greatly under Emer, with abundant resources, animals, cities, and riches. It is described as choice above all other lands and later suffers wickedness, dearth, famine, and poisonous serpents.

l: the curse upon the land, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: The curse upon the land is associated with the people’s iniquity and with the destruction of those who possess the land when they are ripened in iniquity. The Lord begins to take the curse away during Emer’s reign, but prophets later warn that it will return if the people do not repent.

l: the overthrow of Omer's kingdom, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: The overthrow of Omer’s kingdom is caused by the secret combinations of Akish and his friends. Omer escapes after receiving a warning from the Lord, while Jared is made king.

l: the murder of Jared, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: The murder of Jared is carried out by people whom Akish approaches through the oath of the ancients. Jared is killed while sitting on his throne and giving audience to his people.

l: the war between the sons of Akish and Akish, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: The war between the sons of Akish and Akish lasts many years. It results in the destruction of nearly all the people of the kingdom, except for thirty souls and those who flee with the house of Omer.

l: the destruction of nearly all the people, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: The destruction of nearly all the people occurs during the long war between the sons of Akish and Akish. Only thirty souls and those who flee with the house of Omer are spared.

l: the great famine, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: The great famine is prophesied as a consequence of the people’s failure to repent. A dearth later comes upon the land, causing many inhabitants to be destroyed until the people repent and the Lord sends rain.

l: the poisonous serpents, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: The poisonous serpents come upon the land and poison many people. They drive the flocks toward the land southward, and the Lord causes the serpents to hedge up the way so that those attempting to pass may fall by them.

l: the repentance of the people, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: The repentance of the people begins when they see that they must perish and cry unto the Lord. After they humble themselves sufficiently, the Lord sends rain and preserves them from famine.

l: the rain, The Book of Ether, Chapter 9
s: The rain is sent by the Lord after the people humble themselves before him. It causes the people to revive and fruit to appear in the north countries and the surrounding countries.

l: The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: Shez, a descendant of Heth, rebuilt a broken people and established a righteous kingdom, while his eldest son rebelled and was killed by a robber. Riplakish later oppressed the people through heavy taxation, prisons, forced labor, and abominations, leading to rebellion, war, his death, and the expulsion of his descendants. Morianton gained control of the land, eased the people’s burdens, and made them prosperous, but later rulers led the kingdom into captivity until Lib’s reign brought righteousness, industry, commerce, mining, and prosperity. In Lib’s time the poisonous serpents were destroyed, the land northward became densely inhabited, and Com later fought both the king Amgid and organized robbers.

l: Shez (descendant of Heth), The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: Shez was a descendant of Heth, whose household had perished except for Shez. He rebuilt a broken people, built a righteous kingdom, remembered the Lord’s deliverance of Jared and his brother, walked in the Lord’s ways, built many cities, and lived to an exceedingly old age.

l: Riplakish, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: Riplakish reigned after Shez and did not do what was right before the Lord. He had many wives and concubines, imposed heavy taxes, built spacious buildings and prisons, forced people to labor, caused refineries and fine workmanship to be done in prison, and afflicted the people with whoredoms and abominations. After forty-two years, the people rebelled, Riplakish was killed, and his descendants were driven from the land.

l: Morianton, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: Morianton, a descendant of Riplakish, gathered an army of outcasts, fought the people, gained power over the cities and land, and established himself as king. He eased the people’s burden and gained their favor, did justice to the people but not to himself because of his whoredoms, and built many cities. Under his reign the people became exceedingly rich.

l: Lib, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: Lib reigned after Kish and did what was good in the sight of the Lord. In his days the poisonous serpents were destroyed, the people hunted in the land southward, and the land northward became covered with inhabitants. Lib became a great hunter, and he lived many years and begat sons and daughters, including Hearthom.

l: Com, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: Com was begotten by Coriantum and drew away half of the kingdom. He reigned over half of it for forty-two years, fought Amgid for many years, gained power over him and the remainder of the kingdom, and fought against robbers without prevailing over them.

l: people, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: The people were rebuilt under Shez and later spread across the land. They rebelled against Riplakish, fought in wars, prospered under Morianton, and became exceedingly industrious, engaging in trade, mining, crafts, agriculture, animal husbandry, and warfare.

l: robbers, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: Robbers killed Shez’s eldest son because of his exceeding riches. In Com’s days, robbers arose again, adopted the old plans, administered oaths after the manner of the ancients, and sought to destroy the kingdom.

l: the Lord, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: The Lord brought Jared and his brother across the deep, and Shez remembered this deliverance. Shez and later rulers who did what was good or right in the Lord’s sight were favored or prospered, while Morianton was cut off from the Lord’s presence because of his whoredoms.

l: land of promise, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: The land was rebuilt and populated after destruction and war. It contained many cities, abundant animals, ores, fertile areas, and a people who became rich and industrious; it was described as choice above all lands because the Lord had spoken it.

l: the land southward, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: The land southward was preserved as a wilderness for obtaining game. The people went there to hunt food after the poisonous serpents were destroyed.

l: the land northward, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: The whole face of the land northward was covered with inhabitants. It was part of a choice land in which the people prospered and conducted extensive industry and commerce.

l: kingdom, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: Shez built up a righteous kingdom, while Riplakish’s rule ended in rebellion, war, death, and the expulsion of his descendants. Morianton established himself as king over the land, later rulers lost control and served in captivity, and Com eventually obtained power over the remainder of the kingdom after fighting Amgid.

l: cities, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: Shez built many cities, and the people spread over the land. Morianton also built many cities, and Com gained power over many cities during his wars.

l: rebellion against Riplakish, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: After Riplakish had reigned for forty-two years, the people rose up in rebellion against him. War followed, Riplakish was killed, and his descendants were driven out of the land.

l: battle, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: War recurred in the land after the rebellion against Riplakish. Morianton fought for many years to gain control, Levi made war against the king to obtain the kingdom, and Com fought Amgid and the robbers.

l: captivity, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: Kim was brought into captivity by his brother and remained there all his days. His descendants, including Levi’s father, Heth, Aaron, Amnigaddah, and Coriantum, also lived in captivity, while Levi served in captivity for forty-two years before obtaining the kingdom.

l: the reign of Coriantum, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: Riplakish reigned for forty-two years, Morianton reigned after establishing himself as king, Kim reigned eight years, and Com reigned over half the kingdom for forty-two years. Hearthom reigned twenty-four years before the kingdom was taken from him.

l: taxation, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: Riplakish imposed heavy taxes on the people and used the taxes to build many spacious buildings. Those who would not pay or could not pay were cast into prison, and prisoners were forced to labor.

l: prosperity, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: The people became exceedingly rich under Morianton in buildings, gold, silver, grain, flocks, and herds. Under Lib and the following period, they were described as exceedingly blessed and prospered by the hand of the Lord.

l: the poisonous serpents, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: The poisonous serpents were destroyed in the days of Lib. Afterward, the people went into the land southward to hunt food.

l: commerce, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: The people were exceedingly industrious and bought, sold, and trafficked with one another to gain wealth.

l: mining and metallurgy, The Book of Ether, Chapter 10
s: The people worked in every manner of ore and made gold, silver, iron, brass, copper, and other metals. They dug ores from the earth, cast up mighty heaps of earth, refined materials, and produced fine workmanship, tools, weapons, cloth, and other goods.

l: The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: This unit concerns Com, Shiblom, Seth, Ahah, Ethem, Moron, Coriantor, and Ether during the decline and destruction of their people. Prophets repeatedly warned the people to repent of their wickedness, but the people rejected them and followed wicked combinations and secret societies. Wars, calamity, famines, pestilences, rebellion, captivity, and overthrow afflicted the land and its kingdoms. Coriantor died in captivity after begetting Ether, while prophets foretold that the Lord would destroy the people and bring another people to possess the land.

l: Com, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: Com protected prophets who fled to him, and they prophesied many things to him. He was blessed for the remainder of his days, lived to a good old age, and begat Shiblom.

l: prophets, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: The prophets warned of destruction unless the people repented, turned to the Lord, and forsook their murders and wickedness. They were rejected, sought for destruction, put to death, or withdrew from the people, but they continued to prophesy of judgment and another people possessing the land.

l: the Lord, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: The Lord was called upon for repentance, and he had mercy on the people when they repented of their iniquity. The people would not hearken to his voice because of their wicked combinations.

l: people, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: The people rejected and killed or sought to destroy the prophets, hardened their hearts, and would not hearken to prophetic warnings. They suffered wars, famines, pestilences, destruction, and captivity, and some began to repent of their iniquity.

l: the destruction of the people, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: The prophets warned of a great destruction among the people, such as had never been upon the face of the earth, unless they repented. The destruction came through wars, famines, pestilences, and the people's wickedness.

l: repentance, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: The prophets repeatedly called the people to repentance. When the people began to repent of their iniquity, the Lord had mercy on them.

l: wickedness, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: The people were warned to forsake their wickedness and repent of their iniquities. Wickedness continued among their rulers and people and led to bloodshed and destruction.

l: Shiblom, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: Shiblom reigned after Com and was slain during the period of great destruction and calamity.

l: brother of Shiblom, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: The brother of Shiblom rebelled against him and caused the prophets who warned of destruction to be put to death.

l: war, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: An exceedingly great war began throughout the land after the brother of Shiblom rebelled. Wars and contentions later spread through all the land.

l: calamity, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: Great calamity came upon all the land because the people rejected warnings of a curse and destruction.

l: land of promise, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: The land suffered wars, contentions, famines, pestilences, calamity, and great destruction. Prophets warned that a curse would come upon the land unless the people repented.

l: wicked combinations, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: The people did not hearken to the voice of the Lord because of their wicked combinations. These combinations contributed to wars, contentions, and destruction.

l: famines, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: Many famines occurred throughout the land as part of the great destruction that had never been known upon the face of the earth.

l: pestilences, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: Many pestilences occurred throughout the land along with wars and famines, contributing to the great destruction.

l: Seth, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: Seth was brought into captivity and dwelt in captivity all his days.

l: captivity, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: Seth and Moron dwelt in captivity for all their days, and Coriantor also dwelt in captivity all his days.

l: Ahah, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: Ahah, the son of Seth, obtained the kingdom and reigned over the people all his days. He practiced all manner of iniquity, caused much bloodshed, and had few days.

l: Ethem, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: Ethem, a descendant of Ahah, obtained the kingdom and did that which was wicked in his days. During his reign, prophets came and warned the people, and he begat Moron.

l: Moron, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: Moron reigned after Ethem and did that which was wicked before the Lord. He was challenged by a mighty man, later overthrew him and regained the kingdom, and was then overthrown by another mighty man and spent the rest of his days in captivity.

l: rebellion, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: A rebellion arose among the people because of the secret combination built up to obtain power and gain. A mighty man used the rebellion to overthrow half of Moron's kingdom.

l: the secret combinations of Akish and his friends, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: A secret combination was built up to obtain power and gain, causing rebellion among the people. Coriantor's people also rejected the prophets because of their secret society and wicked abominations.

l: mighty man (Moron's challenger), The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: A mighty man arose in iniquity and gave battle to Moron. He overthrew half of the kingdom and maintained it for many years before Moron overthrew him.

l: kingdom, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: The kingdom passed from Com to Shiblom, Seth, Ahah, Ethem, and Moron amid rebellion, overthrow, wickedness, and captivity. Moron's challenger held half of it for many years, and another mighty man later obtained it.

l: overthrow, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: Moron overthrew the mighty man who had taken half of the kingdom and obtained the kingdom again. Another mighty man then overthrew Moron and obtained the kingdom.

l: mighty man (Moron's successor), The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: Another mighty man arose and overthrew Moron, obtaining the kingdom. He was a descendant of the brother of Jared.

l: Coriantor, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: Coriantor was begotten by Moron and dwelt in captivity all his days. During his days, prophets warned of destruction, and he begat Ether before dying in captivity.

l: judgment, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: Prophets warned that the Lord God would execute judgment against the people to their utter destruction unless they repented of their iniquities.

l: another people, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: Prophets warned that the Lord God would send or bring forth another people to possess the land after the manner by which he brought the people's fathers.

l: Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 11
s: Ether was begotten by Coriantor. Coriantor died after dwelling in captivity all his days.

l: The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 12
s: Ether prophesies to the people in the days of Coriantumr, urging them to believe in God and repent. Moroni explains that faith concerns things hoped for and not seen, and that miracles and divine manifestations occur after faith. The Lord teaches Moroni that weakness can become strength through humility and faith, and that faith, hope, and charity lead people to God. Moroni testifies of Jesus Christ and commends the Gentiles to seek Him, with the grace of God, Jesus Christ, and the Holy Ghost abiding in them.

l: Moroni, The Book of Ether, Chapter 12
s: Moroni explains the nature and power of faith, recounts revelations and promises concerning the brother of Jared, and records the Lord’s teachings about weakness, grace, faith, hope, and charity. He prays for the Gentiles, is comforted by the Lord, testifies that he has seen and spoken with Jesus, and commends people to seek Him.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Ether, Chapter 12
s: Jesus Christ shows Himself to people after they have faith, prepares a way for others to partake of the heavenly gift, and speaks with Moroni. Moroni testifies that Jesus loved the world, laid down His life, took it again, and prepared a place for the children of men.

l: God, The Book of Ether, Chapter 12
s: God grants manifestations and miracles according to faith and does not show Himself until after faith. He gives the law of Moses, prepares a more excellent way through the gift of His Son, and works among the children of men according to their faith.

l: the Father, The Book of Ether, Chapter 12
s: The Father is identified as the one whose name Christ glorified and whose mansions contain a prepared place for mankind. Moroni says that charity is required to inherit that place.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Book of Ether, Chapter 12
s: The Holy Ghost enables people to speak much and bears record of God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Moroni asks that it abide in people forever.

l: brother of Jared, The Book of Ether, Chapter 12
s: The brother of Jared has exceedingly great faith and sees the finger of the Lord and all things beyond the veil. His written words are described as mighty, and he commands the mountain Zerin to move, which it does because of his faith.

l: Gentiles, The Book of Ether, Chapter 12
s: The Gentiles may mock the weakness of Moroni’s writing, but the Lord says His grace is sufficient for those who are meek and humble. They are urged to have faith, hope, and charity, and Moroni prays that they may receive grace and charity.

l: children of men, The Book of Ether, Chapter 12
s: The children of men receive weakness so they may be humble, and the Lord can make weak things strong to those who humble themselves and have faith. They must hope to receive an inheritance in the prepared place, and charity is required to inherit it.

l: gift of his Son, The Book of Ether, Chapter 12
s: The gift of His Son provides a more excellent way through which the law is fulfilled and people may partake of the heavenly gift. Partaking of this gift is connected with faith.

l: faith, The Book of Ether, Chapter 12
s: Faith is described as things hoped for and not seen, and people receive no witness until after the trial of their faith. Faith enables people to obtain promises, see divine manifestations, work miracles, and receive strength from weakness.

l: hope, The Book of Ether, Chapter 12
s: Hope comes from faith and provides an anchor to the souls of men, making them sure and steadfast in good works. People must hope to receive an inheritance in the place prepared for them.

l: charity, The Book of Ether, Chapter 12
s: Charity is identified as the love Christ had for the children of men. Without charity, people cannot inherit the place prepared in the mansions of the Father.

l: miracles, The Book of Ether, Chapter 12
s: Miracles are wrought by faith, including the prison’s collapse, the conversion of the Lamanites, and the moving of the mountain Zerin. No one has wrought miracles until after having faith.

l: mansions of my Father, The Book of Ether, Chapter 12
s: The mansions of the Father contain a prepared place where man may have a more excellent hope. Inheritance in that place requires hope and charity.

l: grace of God, The Book of Ether, Chapter 12
s: The grace of God the Father, Jesus Christ, and the Holy Ghost may abide in people forever. The Lord says His grace is sufficient for those who humble themselves before Him.

l: weakness, The Book of Ether, Chapter 12
s: Moroni acknowledges weakness in writing and fears that the Gentiles will mock his words. The Lord says weakness is given so people may be humble and promises to make weak things strong when they humble themselves and have faith.

l: The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: Moroni finishes his record about the destruction of the people and recounts Ether’s prophecies concerning this land, the New Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the house of Israel, and the remnant of the seed of Joseph. Ether was rejected and expelled, hid in the cavity of a rock, and recorded the destruction he saw. Coriantumr and the people continued in war and wickedness despite Ether’s warning that repentance would spare them. Shared temporarily captured Coriantumr, but Coriantumr’s sons restored the kingdom, and Coriantumr later killed Shared before being wounded and unable to fight for two years.

l: Moroni, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: Moroni proceeds to finish his record concerning the destruction of the people about whom he has been writing.

l: Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: Ether prophesies about Christ, this land, the New Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the house of Israel, and the remnant of the seed of Joseph. The people reject him and cast him out, after which he hides in the cavity of a rock and records the destructions he observes.

l: Coriantumr, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: Coriantumr studies the arts of war and the cunning of the world and fights those seeking to destroy him. He refuses to repent, is captured by Shared and later freed by his sons, kills Shared, and is wounded in the thigh so that he cannot fight for two years.

l: the Lord, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: The Lord sends his word to Ether, directing him to prophesy that Coriantumr and his household must repent or the people and household will be destroyed.

l: people, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: The people reject Ether’s words and continue in war, secret violence, robbery, and wickedness. Many are slain, and there is none to restrain the bloodshed.

l: the house of Israel, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: The house of Israel is connected with Jerusalem, the remnant of the seed of Joseph, and the fulfilling of the covenant made with Abraham.

l: the remnant of the seed of Joseph, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: The remnant of the seed of Joseph is to inherit this land and build a holy city unto the Lord. They are identified with those who dwell in the New Jerusalem and whose garments are white through the blood of the Lamb.

l: the secret combinations of Akish and his friends, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: Secret combinations are involved in the fighting against Coriantumr, and many people are slain by their sword.

l: New Jerusalem, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: The New Jerusalem is to come down out of heaven and be a holy sanctuary of the Lord. It is to be built upon this land for the remnant of the seed of Joseph, and those who dwell there are blessed.

l: Jerusalem, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: Jerusalem, from whence Lehi should come, is to be destroyed and built up again as a holy city unto the Lord. Its inhabitants are described as scattered and gathered from the four quarters of the earth and as partakers of the covenant made with Abraham.

l: land of promise, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: This land becomes a choice land above all other lands and a chosen land of the Lord. The New Jerusalem is to be built upon it for the remnant of the seed of Joseph.

l: the cavity of a rock, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: The cavity of a rock is where Ether hides by day after being cast out and where he makes the remainder of his record while viewing the destructions by night.

l: the record of Moroni, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: The record of Moroni concerns the destruction of the people, and Moroni proceeds to finish it in this unit.

l: the prophecies of Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: The prophecies of Ether are described as great and marvelous and concern Christ, the New Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the house of Israel, and the destruction of the people.

l: the words of Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: The people reject all the words of Ether, although he tells them of the history and destiny of this land and warns them of what will come.

l: the New Jerusalem prophecy, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: The New Jerusalem prophecy states that a New Jerusalem will be built upon this land for the remnant of the seed of Joseph and that it will be a holy city of the Lord.

l: the covenant God made with Abraham, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: The covenant God made with Abraham is fulfilled for those who were scattered and gathered from the four quarters of the earth and from the north countries.

l: the blood of the Lamb, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: The blood of the Lamb makes the garments of those in the New Jerusalem white and washes the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

l: the destruction of the people, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: The destruction of the people is the subject of Moroni’s record and of Ether’s observations from the cavity of a rock. Ether warns that the people and Coriantumr’s household will be destroyed if they do not repent.

l: Ether's expulsion, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: Ether is cast out from among the people after they reject his prophecies. He hides in the cavity of a rock and continues making his record.

l: the great war, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: The great war begins in the year Ether is cast out, as mighty men rise against Coriantumr with secret plans of wickedness.

l: war, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: The wars continue because Coriantumr, his household, and the people do not repent. They include battles involving Coriantumr and Shared and eventually spread across the whole land.

l: repentance, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: Ether is told to warn Coriantumr that repentance by him and all his household would bring the kingdom and spare the people. Coriantumr, his household, and the people do not repent.

l: wickedness, The Book of Ether, Chapter 13
s: Wickedness includes secret plans, robbery, and all manner of wrongdoing across the land. The people continue in wickedness without repentance.

l: The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 14
s: A curse came upon all the land because of the iniquity of the people, causing tools and swords to disappear and people to guard their property. Coriantumr fought the brother of Shared, Gilead, Lib, and Shiz in a prolonged succession of battles, gaining and losing ground across the land. Lib, a man of great stature, became king after a secret combination murdered Gilead, but Coriantumr later killed Lib. Shiz then pursued Coriantumr, and the war caused widespread destruction, death, famine-like disturbance from the scent of unburied bodies, and the deaths of men, women, and children.

l: Coriantumr, The Book of Ether, Chapter 14
s: Coriantumr fought the brother of Shared, Gilead, and Lib, defeating and pursuing them at different times. He killed Lib on the plains of Agosh, then fled before Shiz until the armies fought for three days by the seashore and later at hill Comnor. Shiz inflicted many deep wounds on him, causing him to faint and be carried away as though dead.

l: Lib, The Book of Ether, Chapter 14
s: Lib was a man of great stature, more than any other man among all the people. After a secret combination murdered Gilead, Lib obtained the kingdom and fought Coriantumr. Coriantumr smote him on the plains of Agosh until he died.

l: people, The Book of Ether, Chapter 14
s: The people guarded their property and lives because of the curse upon the land. They joined the armies of Shiz or Coriantumr, and many people were killed, displaced, or swept away during the war.

l: secret combinations, The Book of Ether, Chapter 14
s: Secret combinations gave Gilead great strength to his army. One of the secret combinations murdered Gilead in a secret pass and obtained the kingdom for Lib.

l: army of Coriantumr, The Book of Ether, Chapter 14
s: The army of Coriantumr pursued the brother of Shared and later fought Lib and Shiz. It received great strength while dwelling in the wilderness, but was repeatedly driven back before defeating Lib and later causing Shiz's people to flee.

l: people of Shiz, The Book of Ether, Chapter 14
s: The army of Shiz pursued Coriantumr, overthrew cities, and killed women and children. It fought Coriantumr's army at the seashore and hill Comnor, inflicted many wounds on Coriantumr, and eventually returned to its camp without pursuing his armies.

l: land of promise, The Book of Ether, Chapter 14
s: A great curse came upon all the land because of the iniquity of the people. The land was covered with the bodies of the dead, and the scent of the bodies troubled the people by day and by night.

l: the curse upon the land, The Book of Ether, Chapter 14
s: The curse upon the land caused a man's tool or sword to disappear when left on a shelf or other place. Because of it, every man held tightly to his own property and would not borrow or lend.

l: war, The Book of Ether, Chapter 14
s: The war between the armies of Shiz and Coriantumr was so great and lasting that the whole face of the land was covered with dead bodies. The armies moved from one shedding of blood to another, leaving men, women, and children unburied.

l: battles against Jared, The Book of Ether, Chapter 14
s: Battles occurred between Coriantumr and the brother of Shared, Gilead, Lib, and Shiz. The battle at hill Comnor became exceedingly sore, and Shiz gave Coriantumr many deep wounds.

l: bloodshed and carnage, The Book of Ether, Chapter 14
s: The bloodshed and carnage lasted so long and was so extensive that no one remained to bury the dead. The bodies of men, women, and children were left scattered across the land.

l: destruction, The Book of Ether, Chapter 14
s: The destruction among the armies of Shiz became so terrible that the people were frightened and fled before Coriantumr's armies. The destruction also included cities being overthrown and burned and women and children being slain.

l: The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 15
s: Coriantumr remembered Ether’s words, mourned the destruction of nearly two million people, repented, and asked Shiz to spare the people. Shiz refused unless Coriantumr surrendered, and the people of Coriantumr and the people of Shiz continued gathering for battle. After years of preparation, the armies fought until nearly all were slain, leaving only Coriantumr and Shiz, who fought until Coriantumr killed Shiz and then collapsed. The Lord told Ether to go forth, and Ether saw that the Lord’s words had been fulfilled and finished his record.

l: Coriantumr, The Book of Ether, Chapter 15
s: Coriantumr recovered from his wounds, remembered Ether’s words and the prophets, sorrowed over the deaths of nearly two million people, and repented of his evil. He wrote to Shiz asking him to spare the people and offered to give up the kingdom. Coriantumr led his people in repeated battles, killed Shiz, and then fell to the earth as if lifeless.

l: Shiz, The Book of Ether, Chapter 15
s: Shiz refused to spare the people unless Coriantumr gave himself up so that Shiz could kill him. He led his people in repeated battles against the people of Coriantumr and pursued Coriantumr after his army fled. Shiz was eventually killed by Coriantumr after fainting from loss of blood.

l: Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 15
s: Ether’s words were remembered by Coriantumr. Ether observed the doings of the people, saw that the Lord’s words had been fulfilled, finished his record, and hid it where the people of Limhi found it.

l: the Lord, The Book of Ether, Chapter 15
s: The Lord’s words were fulfilled as Ether observed the destruction of the people. The Lord spoke to Ether and told him to go forth.

l: people of Coriantumr, The Book of Ether, Chapter 15
s: The people of Coriantumr were stirred to anger against the people of Shiz and fought them. They gathered for four years, including their wives and children, and continued fighting until nearly all had fallen by the sword.

l: people of Shiz, The Book of Ether, Chapter 15
s: The people of Shiz were stirred to anger against the people of Coriantumr and gave battle to them. They gathered for four years with their wives and children and fought until nearly all had fallen by the sword.

l: people, The Book of Ether, Chapter 15
s: The people did not repent of their iniquity. They gathered into opposing armies, fought for many days, and were destroyed until only a few remained.

l: battle, The Book of Ether, Chapter 15
s: The battle between the people of Coriantumr and the people of Shiz continued for years of gathering and then through repeated days of fighting. The armies suffered immense losses, and the final battle ended with Coriantumr killing Shiz.

l: death, The Book of Ether, Chapter 15
s: Death came to nearly two million people, including mighty men, their wives, and their children. Continued battles left only Coriantumr and Shiz, and Shiz died after Coriantumr smote off his head.

l: The Book of Moroni, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 1
s: Moroni says he has finished abridging the account of the people of Jared but continues to live and write. He hides his identity from the Lamanites because they may kill him, and he wanders for safety. The Lamanites fight fiercely among themselves and kill Nephites who will not deny Christ. Moroni refuses to deny Christ and writes additional things that may someday benefit the Lamanites.

l: Moroni, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 1
s: Moroni has finished abridging the account of the people of Jared but continues to live and write. He refuses to deny Christ, hides from the Lamanites, wanders for safety, and writes additional things for his brethren, the Lamanites.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 1
s: The Lamanites are engaged in exceedingly fierce wars among themselves. They kill every Nephite who will not deny Christ, and Moroni avoids revealing himself to them because they may destroy him.

l: wars, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 1
s: The wars are exceedingly fierce among the Lamanites and occur among themselves.

l: Nephites, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 1
s: The Lamanites put to death every Nephite who will not deny Christ.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 1
s: Moroni will not deny Christ. The Lamanites kill Nephites who refuse to deny Christ.

l: The Book of Moroni, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 2
s: Christ gives his twelve chosen disciples instructions about prayer and giving the Holy Ghost. He tells them to call on the Father in his name in mighty prayer and says they will have power to give the Holy Ghost by laying hands on people. The multitude does not hear these words, but the disciples do, and the Holy Ghost falls on as many as they lay their hands upon.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 2
s: Christ speaks to his twelve chosen disciples, instructing them to call on the Father in his name and to give the Holy Ghost by laying hands on people.

l: disciples (Christ's disciples), The Book of Moroni, Chapter 2
s: The disciples hear Christ's words, call on the Father in Christ's name, and lay their hands on people, upon whom the Holy Ghost falls.

l: God, the Eternal Father, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 2
s: The Father is the one whom the disciples are instructed to call on in Christ's name in mighty prayer.

l: Holy Ghost, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 2
s: The Holy Ghost is given by the disciples in Christ's name, and it falls on as many people as the disciples lay their hands upon.

l: multitude, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 2
s: The multitude does not hear Christ's words when he speaks them to the disciples.

l: The Book of Moroni, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 3
s: The disciples, who were called the elders of the church, ordained priests and teachers. After praying to the Father in the name of Jesus Christ, they laid their hands upon those being ordained. Priests and teachers were ordained to preach repentance and remission of sins through Jesus Christ by the endurance of faith on his name to the end. They were ordained according to the gifts and callings of God unto men by the power of the Holy Ghost.

l: disciples (elders of the church), The Book of Moroni, Chapter 3
s: The disciples, who were called the elders of the church, prayed to the Father in the name of Jesus Christ, laid their hands upon those being ordained, and ordained priests and teachers.

l: priests, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 3
s: Priests were ordained to preach repentance and remission of sins through Jesus Christ by the endurance of faith on his name to the end.

l: teachers, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 3
s: Teachers were ordained to preach repentance and remission of sins through Jesus Christ by the endurance of faith on his name to the end.

l: God, the Eternal Father, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 3
s: The Father was prayed to in the name of Jesus Christ before priests and teachers were ordained.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 3
s: Jesus Christ was named in the prayer to the Father and in the instruction for priests and teachers to preach repentance and remission of sins through him.

l: Holy Ghost, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 3
s: The Holy Ghost was in the disciples and gave the power by which they ordained priests and teachers.

l: ordination, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 3
s: Ordination involved prayer to the Father in the name of Jesus Christ, laying hands upon those being ordained, and speaking the appropriate ordaining words. Priests and teachers were ordained according to the gifts and callings of God unto men by the power of the Holy Ghost.

l: The Book of Moroni, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 4
s: Elders and priests administer the flesh and blood of Christ to the church according to the commandments of Christ. The elder or priest kneels with the church and prays to God, the Eternal Father, in the name of Jesus Christ. The prayer asks that the bread be blessed and sanctified so participants remember the body of Jesus Christ, take upon themselves his name, keep his commandments, and have his Spirit with them.

l: elders, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 4
s: Elders administer the flesh and blood of Christ to the church according to the commandments of Christ.

l: priests, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 4
s: Priests administer the flesh and blood of Christ to the church according to the commandments of Christ.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 4
s: Jesus Christ is named as the Son in whose name the prayer is offered. His commandments are to be kept, and his name is to be taken upon the participants.

l: flesh and blood of Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 4
s: The flesh and blood of Christ are administered to the church according to the commandments of Christ.

l: church of Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 4
s: The church receives the administration of the flesh and blood of Christ. The church kneels with the elder or priest during the prayer.

l: commandments of Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 4
s: The commandments of Christ govern the administration of the flesh and blood of Christ. Participants witness that they are willing to keep these commandments.

l: bread, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 4
s: Bread is prayed over so that it may be blessed and sanctified to the souls of all who partake of it. Those who eat it are to remember the body of Jesus Christ.

l: body of Jesus Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 4
s: The body of Jesus Christ is to be remembered by those who partake of the bread.

l: Holy Ghost, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 4
s: The Spirit is to be with those who take upon themselves the name of Jesus Christ, remember him, and keep his commandments.

l: administering the flesh and blood of Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 4
s: Administering the flesh and blood of Christ is done by an elder or priest according to the commandments of Christ.

l: prayer to God, the Eternal Father, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 4
s: The prayer to God, the Eternal Father, is offered by the elder or priest while kneeling with the church and is made in the name of Jesus Christ.

l: The Book of Moroni, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 5
s: The unit describes the manner of administering the wine. The participants take the cup and ask God, the Eternal Father, in the name of Jesus Christ, to bless and sanctify the wine. The wine is intended to be consumed in remembrance of the blood of Jesus Christ, which was shed for them. Those who drink are to witness that they always remember Jesus Christ and may have his Spirit with them.

l: wine, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 5
s: The wine is blessed and sanctified for the souls of those who drink it. They drink it in remembrance of the blood of Jesus Christ, which was shed for them.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 5
s: Jesus Christ is named as the Son in whose name the prayer is offered. His blood was shed for those who drink the wine, who are to consume it in remembrance of him.

l: souls (of those who drink the wine), The Book of Moroni, Chapter 5
s: The wine is blessed and sanctified to the souls of those who drink it. They are to drink it in remembrance of the blood of Jesus Christ and witness that they always remember him.

l: Holy Ghost, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 5
s: Those who drink the wine may have Jesus Christ's Spirit to be with them.

l: The Book of Moroni, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 6
s: This unit concerns baptism and the practices governing membership in the church of Christ. Elders, priests, teachers, and others are baptized only after bringing forth worthy fruit, showing a broken heart and contrite spirit, witnessing true repentance, and taking upon themselves the name of Christ. Members are numbered, remembered, nourished, and instructed to meet often to fast, pray, speak about their souls, and partake of bread and wine in remembrance of the Lord Jesus. The church removes names for unrepented iniquity but forgives those who repent and seek forgiveness with real intent, and its meetings follow the workings and power of the Holy Ghost.

l: baptism, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 6
s: Baptism is given only to those who bring forth worthy fruit, have a broken heart and contrite spirit, witness that they have truly repented of all their sins, and determine to serve Christ to the end.

l: church of Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 6
s: The church of Christ numbers baptized people among its members, takes their names so they may be remembered and nourished by the good word of God, and meets often to care for their souls. It observes that there should be no iniquity among its members, blots out the names of those who do not repent and confess, and forgives those who repent and seek forgiveness with real intent.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 6
s: Christ is the one whose name those baptized take upon themselves and whom they determine to serve to the end. His merits are relied upon alone, and he is the author and finisher of their faith.

l: Holy Ghost, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 6
s: The Holy Ghost cleanses those received unto baptism and leads the church's meetings. By its power, the church preaches, exhorts, prays, supplicates, and sings.

l: repentance, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 6
s: Repentance is witnessed before baptism, and those who commit iniquity must repent and confess or have their names blotted out. Those who repent and seek forgiveness with real intent are forgiven.

l: prayer, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 6
s: The church meets often to fast and pray, and its members are kept continually watchful unto prayer while relying upon the merits of Christ.

l: meetings, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 6
s: The church's meetings occur often for fasting, prayer, discussion about the welfare of souls, and partaking of bread and wine in remembrance of the Lord Jesus. They are conducted according to the workings and power of the Holy Ghost.

l: The Book of Moroni, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: Mormon teaches the church about judging good and evil, faith in Jesus Christ, hope through Christ’s atonement and resurrection, and charity as the pure love of Christ. He explains that all good things come from God through Christ, while evil comes from the devil. He teaches that faith enables miracles, angelic ministry, salvation, and becoming the sons of God. He urges the people to pray for charity and to remain meek, lowly, faithful, hopeful, and charitable.

l: Mormon, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: Mormon teaches the peaceable followers of Christ about good and evil, faith, hope, and charity. He urges them to judge by the light of Christ, seek every good thing, and pray to be filled with the pure love of Christ.

l: God, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: God permits Mormon to speak and gives the Spirit of Christ to every person so they may know good from evil. All things that are good come from God, and God sends angels and prophets to reveal the coming of Christ.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: Jesus Christ is the source of every good thing and saves people who have faith in his name. He claims those who have faith in him, advocates for the children of men, calls them to repentance and baptism, and grants power to those who have faith in him.

l: Holy Ghost, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: The Holy Ghost may have place in the hearts of the children of men according to its power. Through the power of the Holy Ghost, a meek and lowly person may confess that Jesus is the Christ.

l: Spirit of Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: The Spirit of Christ is given to every man so that each may know good from evil. It shows that whatever invites people to do good and believe in Christ is of God.

l: devil, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: The devil is an enemy to God who continually fights against him and entices people to sin and do evil. The devil cannot persuade anyone to do good, and a person who follows Christ cannot be a servant of the devil.

l: angels, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: Angels minister to the children of men according to Christ’s command and appear to people with strong faith and a firm mind in godliness. Their ministry calls people to repentance, fulfills the Father’s covenants, and declares the word of Christ.

l: children of men, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: The children of men receive good things through Christ and may be ministered to by angels. They can gain faith, receive the Holy Ghost, be saved through faith in Christ, and become the sons of God.

l: church of Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: The church consists of peaceable followers of Christ who have hope sufficient to enter into the rest of the Lord. Those without faith in Christ are not fit to be numbered among its people.

l: faith, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: Faith in Christ enables people to lay hold upon every good thing, receive answers to prayer, perform miracles, and receive angelic ministry. Faith is necessary for hope and salvation, and it is shown through meekness.

l: hope, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: Hope is attained through faith and comes through the atonement of Christ and the power of his resurrection. It is hope of being raised to eternal life according to the promise.

l: charity, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: Charity is the pure love of Christ and is patient, kind, humble, truthful, enduring, and unfailing. Without charity a person is nothing, while those who possess it at the last day will fare well.

l: good and evil, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: Good comes from God and evil comes from the devil. The Spirit of Christ provides a clear way to distinguish them, and people are warned not to judge good as evil or evil as good.

l: mighty miracles, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: Miracles have not ceased because Christ has ascended into heaven. They are wrought by faith, and if they cease it is because of unbelief.

l: atonement of Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: The atonement of Christ provides the basis for hope of being raised to eternal life. Christ answered the ends of the law and claims all who have faith in him.

l: resurrection, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: The power of Christ’s resurrection enables people to be raised unto life eternal through faith in him. Hope for eternal life rests on this power and the promise.

l: salvation, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 7
s: People are saved by faith in the name of Jesus Christ. Without faith, people would be as though no redemption had been made.

l: The Book of Moroni, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 8
s: Mormon writes an epistle to his son Moroni after Moroni’s calling to the ministry. He teaches that little children are alive in Christ, cannot commit sin or repent, and do not need baptism. Mormon condemns baptizing little children as a denial of the mercies and power of Jesus Christ, and teaches that baptism and repentance are for those accountable and capable of committing sin. He also warns that the Nephites are in danger because they reject God, the Holy Ghost, and prophetic teachings.

l: Mormon, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 8
s: Mormon writes to Moroni, rejoicing in his calling and praying for him. He teaches against the baptism of little children and warns the Nephites to repent because of their pride, rejection of God’s power, and denial of the Holy Ghost.

l: Moroni, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 8
s: Moroni receives Mormon’s epistle soon after being called to the ministry. Mormon asks him to labor diligently to remove the error of baptizing little children and to pray for the Nephites.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 8
s: Jesus Christ is identified as the Redeemer, Lord, and God. Mormon teaches that little children are whole through Christ, that the curse of Adam has no power over them, and that baptism is for repentance and remission of sins.

l: God, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 8
s: God the Father is addressed in prayer in the name of Jesus. Mormon teaches that God is not partial or changeable and that His mercy saves little children and those without the law.

l: Holy Ghost, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 8
s: The word of the Lord comes to Mormon by the power of the Holy Ghost. The Holy Ghost later visits those who repent, bringing hope and perfect love, while the Nephites are accused of denying the Holy Ghost.

l: little children, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 8
s: Little children are described as whole, unable to commit sin or repent, and alive in Christ from the foundation of the world. They need neither repentance nor baptism and are all alike and partakers of salvation.

l: baptism, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 8
s: Baptism is taught as belonging to repentance and the fulfillment of commandments for those accountable and capable of committing sin. Baptizing little children is called solemn mockery before God and a denial of Christ’s mercies.

l: repentance, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 8
s: Repentance is for those under condemnation and the curse of a broken law. Its first fruits are baptism, and it leads through remission of sins to meekness, the visitation of the Holy Ghost, hope, and perfect love.

l: The Book of Moroni, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: The writer tells his son that he is alive but describes a failed battle with the Lamanites, the deaths of important men, and the loss of many choice men. He reports that both the Lamanites and their own people have committed extreme cruelty against prisoners, women, and children, and that their people have become without order, mercy, principle, and feeling. The writer fears that the Lord’s Spirit has ceased striving with them and that the people will be destroyed unless they repent and return to God. He urges his son to remain faithful in Christ and recommends him to God, trusting in Christ’s mercy and eternal life.

l: Moroni, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: The son receives a letter from the writer describing the failed battle, the sufferings and wickedness of the people, and the danger of destruction. The writer urges him to labor diligently, remain faithful in Christ, and not be weighed down by the things written. The writer recommends him to God and hopes to see him again and deliver sacred records to him.

l: writer (the speaker), The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: The writer says that he is still alive but is writing about grievous matters. He has had a sore battle with the Lamanites, cannot any longer enforce his commands because his people have become strong in perversion, and fears for their destruction. He continues laboring with them, prays for his son, and trusts in Christ.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: The Lamanites defeated the writer’s people in a sore battle and took many prisoners from the tower of Sherrizah. They killed the husbands and fathers of women and children, fed the prisoners the flesh of their slain relatives, and gave them very little water. They also took many daughters of the Lamanites’ enemies, violated their chastity and virtue, tortured and murdered them, and devoured their flesh.

l: Satan, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: Satan continually stirs the people up to anger one with another.

l: our people, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: The people do not repent, have lost their love for one another, and thirst continually after blood and revenge. They have committed abominations against prisoners, including violating, torturing, murdering, and devouring the daughters of the Lamanites. They are described as without order, mercy, principle, and feeling, and their wickedness exceeds that of the Lamanites.

l: God, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: God is asked to come out in judgment against the people and to hide their sins, wickedness, and abominations from before his face. The writer cannot recommend the people to God lest God smite him, but recommends his son to God and prays that God will spare his life.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: The writer trusts in Christ that his son will be saved and urges him to be faithful in Christ. He asks that Christ lift his son up and that the hope of Christ’s glory and eternal life remain in his mind.

l: Lord, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: The Lord Jesus Christ is described as sitting on the right hand of God’s power until all things become subject unto him. The writer prays that the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ will be and abide with them forever.

l: Sherrizah, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: Sherrizah is a tower from which the Lamanites took many men, women, and children as prisoners. Widows and their daughters remain there, while provisions left behind by the Lamanites were carried away by the army of Zenephi, leaving them to wander for food. Many old women faint and die along the way.

l: kingdom of God, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: The writer says that he and his son have a labor to perform while in the tabernacle of clay so that they may conquer the enemy of all righteousness and rest their souls in the kingdom of God.

l: sore battle with the Lamanites, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: The sore battle with the Lamanites was not conquered by the writer’s people. Archeantus, Luram, and Emron fell by the sword, and many choice men were lost.

l: destruction of the people, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: The writer fears that the Lamanites will destroy the people because they do not repent and are continually stirred up to anger. He says that the people must perish unless they repent and return unto God, and that their destruction may resemble that of the Jaredites.

l: sufferings of the people, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: The sufferings of the people include captivity, starvation, killings, cruelty, and the abandonment of women, children, and old women. The writer says that the suffering of the women and children across the land exceeds everything that can be told or written.

l: repentance, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: The people do not repent, and the writer fears that the Spirit of the Lord has ceased striving with them. He says they will perish except they repent and return unto God.

l: blood and revenge, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: The people have lost their love for one another and thirst continually after blood and revenge. Their wilfulness in seeking blood and revenge is compared to that of the Jaredites.

l: return of the people unto God, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: The writer hopes that his son may live to witness the return of the people unto God or their utter destruction. He states that the people must perish unless they repent and return unto God.

l: sufferings and death of Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 9
s: The writer asks that Christ’s sufferings and death, together with the showing of his body unto their fathers, his mercy and long-suffering, and the hope of his glory and eternal life, remain in his son’s mind forever.

l: The Book of Moroni, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: Moroni writes to the Lamanites and seals up the records more than four hundred and twenty years after the sign of the coming of Christ. He exhorts readers to remember the Lord’s mercy, ask God in the name of Christ with sincere faith, and learn truth by the power of the Holy Ghost. He teaches that gifts of God come through the Spirit of Christ and that faith, hope, and charity are necessary for salvation in the kingdom of God. He calls all people to come unto Christ, receive grace, deny ungodliness, and become holy through the blood of Christ, and he bids farewell until his spirit and body reunite.

l: Moroni, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: Moroni writes to the Lamanites, seals up the records, exhorts readers to remember the Lord’s mercy, and declares that God will show that what he has written is true. He says he will soon go to rest in the paradise of God until his spirit and body reunite and he is brought forth triumphant to meet others before the bar of the great Jehovah.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: The Lamanites are the people to whom Moroni writes, and they are exhorted to receive and consider the records.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: Christ is acknowledged by every good thing, and people may know that he is by the power of the Holy Ghost. Christ gives spiritual gifts, teaches that faith enables people to do what is expedient, and calls people to come unto him and be perfected in him.

l: Lord, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: The Lord is described as having been merciful unto the children of men from the creation of Adam until the time when they receive the records.

l: God, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: God is asked for truth in the name of Christ, and he manifests truth by the power of the Holy Ghost. God gives gifts, works according to faith, and shows that Moroni’s writing is true.

l: God, the Eternal Father, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: The Eternal Father is addressed as God, and his covenants with the house of Israel are to be fulfilled.

l: Holy Ghost, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: The Holy Ghost manifests the truth to those who ask with a sincere heart, real intent, and faith in Christ. By the power of the Holy Ghost, people may know the truth of all things and that Christ is.

l: children of men, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: The children of men receive the Lord’s mercy, and spiritual gifts are given to them according to their faith. Their unbelief can cause the gifts and power of God to be done away, and despair comes because of iniquity.

l: house of Israel, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: The house of Israel is called to awake and arise from the dust, put on beautiful garments, strengthen its stakes, enlarge its borders, and receive fulfillment of the covenants of the Eternal Father.

l: Jerusalem, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: Jerusalem is called to awake and arise from the dust and put on its beautiful garments.

l: Zion, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: Zion is addressed as the daughter of Zion and is called to put on beautiful garments, strengthen its stakes, and enlarge its borders forever.

l: records, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: Moroni seals up the records after exhorting the Lamanites. Readers are asked to remember the Lord’s mercy and ponder the records in their hearts.

l: words of Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: The words of Christ declare that if people have faith, they can do all things which are expedient unto Christ. Moroni says the words written by him will be declared at the bar of God.

l: coming of Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: More than four hundred and twenty years have passed since the sign was given of the coming of Christ.

l: gifts of God, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: The gifts of God are many and come from the same God through different ways of administration. They include wisdom, knowledge, faith, healing, miracles, prophecy, the beholding of angels and ministering spirits, tongues, and interpretation of languages and tongues; they continue as long as the world stands except according to unbelief.

l: faith, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: Faith in Christ, together with a sincere heart and real intent, enables people to know truth through the Holy Ghost. Faith is required for salvation in the kingdom of God and allows people to do all things which are expedient unto Christ.

l: hope, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: Hope is required where there is faith, and without hope a person must be in despair. Despair comes because of iniquity.

l: charity, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: Charity is required where there are faith and hope. Without charity, a person cannot be saved in the kingdom of God.
